q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a petrol pump or fuel station?
title: Fuel station carbon footprint
short: A fuel station's own footprint is its electricity for dispensers, lights and the convenience store at 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, plus generator diesel. The fuel it sells is not its Scope 1: customers burning it fall under Scope 3, Category 11, for sold fuels.
audience: Fuel station dealers and oil marketing company outlets

ul: Electricity for dispensers, canopy lights, air compressors and the store.
Diesel used in the station generator.

p: The Scope 3 Standard puts the combustion of sold fuels in Category 11. For a dealer it is many times larger than the station's own footprint, so report it separately and say whose fuel it is.
Evaporation of petrol releases volatile organic compounds, which are not among the greenhouse gases the GHG Protocol counts.

example.title: Worked example: one fuel station (one month, illustrative inputs)
lines: Station Scope 1 and 2: 1,989.4 kg CO2 a month
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use the station electricity bill and generator log.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
